findings.summary: CLOSED: the provider-failure test now exercises a real failure; stale-usable and expired reader boundaries are covered.
findings.detail: The inert fresh-cache test was replaced/renamed. RadarrCacheHitAvoidsAnyProviderCall covers the fresh hit; RadarrStaleObservationSetIsServedWithoutAProviderCallWhenTheProviderFails stores an entry observed 45s ago under a 1-minute TTL (fresh for 30s, stale-but-usable until 60s per ArrInventoryCacheEntry.ComputeFreshnessWindow) with a failing responder and asserts success, the quality label, an empty request list, and count 1 — so a provider failure is present while a usable entry is served as bounded last-known-good. RadarrExpiredObservationSetIsEvictedAndTheProviderFailureIsBounded stores at -90s (>TTL), asserts the provider was actually read once, the bounded ProviderUnavailable/Later failure is returned, and the expired entry is not retained. The direct construction at chosen observation times supplies the missing clock seam (worker limitation #2) at the reader boundary. Both are mutation-sensitive: making IsExpired always false fails the expired test.

findings.summary: CLOSED: per-connection single-flight coalescing is implemented and verified under a real concurrent cold start.
findings.detail: ArrInventoryCacheProvider owns a per-connection SemaphoreSlim(1,1) population gate. On a cold cache the readers acquire the gate, re-check the cache inside it, and only then read the library, so concurrent readers for the connection share one library read; a waiter re-checks and serves from the populated set. The gate is an async semaphore, so no thread is blocked and no monitor lock is held across provider I/O; WaitAsync is cancellation-aware; the lease is disposed on every path via using so a provider failure or cancellation releases the gate and does not poison later attempts; a failed population does not share failure but later attempts retry (documented). ConcurrentColdReadersShareOneLibraryRead launches four cold readers against a blocking handler and asserts LibraryRequestCount == 1; ProviderFailureReleasesThePopulationGateForALaterAttempt drives a failed population then a successful later attempt. I ran both plus the stale-entry test 8 consecutive times (all green), so the concurrency coverage is deterministic here. With the gate, the declaration 'one provider library read per connection serves a reconciliation window' is now literally true under concurrent cold start, not only against a populated cache.
evidence: 8x focused run of ConcurrentColdReadersShareOneLibraryRead + ProviderFailureReleasesThePopulationGateForALaterAttempt + RadarrStaleObservationSet... -> Passed 3/3 each time
findings.recommended_action: None; closed. (The earlier 11.2-F2 adjudication that this was an acceptable bounded deviation is superseded by this implementation.)

findings.summary: Bulk id lists are now chunked into bounded requests; a residual theoretical bound remains at the maximum configurable batch size.
findings.detail: RadarrClient.GetMovieFilesAsync(IReadOnlyList<int>) and SonarrClient.GetEpisodeFilesAsync(IReadOnlyList<int>) now chunk the id list by OperationalLimits.ReconciliationBatchSize (default 100, validated 1-1000) and merge the chunk results, so the default request line stays well under typical limits and a large library no longer emits one unbounded query. BulkReadsChunkTheIdListIntoBoundedRequests sets ReconciliationBatchSize=1 and asserts one request per id with the expected query values. Residual, non-blocking: at the maximum validated ReconciliationBatchSize=1000 an id query is ~12 KB, which could still exceed a proxy/server request-line limit; correctness is preserved by the existing direct-read fallback. This was a LOW, explicitly non-blocking follow-up in attempt 1, and the correction addressed it as claimed.

findings.summary: The single-flight gate is an async semaphore intentionally held across provider I/O; the per-connection gate dictionary is bounded by configured connections.
findings.detail: The reviewer constraint 'no lock held across provider I/O' is satisfied: the only monitor lock (ArrInventoryCacheProvider._gate) guards cache resolution and is never held across I/O; the SemaphoreSlim is the intended single-flight lease and is necessarily held across the population. WaitAsync is cancellation-aware and the lease is released on every path. _populationGates is a ConcurrentDictionary keyed by ArrConnectionId and grows only with the configured connection count, not per request. No deadlock path exists because the population path never re-acquires the gate.
